Explain the example for build your first less file

blocks.text: Less is a CSS helper language. A compiler translates its extra features into the CSS that browsers already understand.
Use Less 4 on your computer. Install Node.js first. Save examples as lesson.less, then run npx lessc lesson.less lesson.css. The browser loads lesson.css; this site does not build Less.
Read the code step by step

items: `less@4` chooses the major version used in these lessons.
`lessc --version` checks the compiler; compiling a file is a separate command.

blocks.text: Less is added to the project. The version command confirms that the tool can run.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Installing the tool does not add styles to a page. You must build a CSS file and link that file from HTML.
